question: What are the performance/cost tradeoffs between `searchBySummarization: 'page'` vs other summarization strategies in `queryGroup`?

searches.query: advanced LLM prompt configuration summarize document context

searchBySummarization_parameter.description: (Recommended) Configure this to search for context using summaries of document chunks. If you set `page`, each page is a chunk. If you set `outline`, an LLM outlines the document, and each segment of the outline is a chunk. This parameter is compatible with documents up to 1,280 pages long.
searchBySummarization_parameter.interactions: If you configure this parameter for a document 5 pages or under in length, Sensible submits the entire document as context, bypassing summarization. If you configure this parameter for a document over 5 pages long, then Sensible sets the Chunk Count parameter to 5 and ignores any configured value.

default_approach.name: Locate context with embeddings scores
default_approach.description: Splits document into equally sized chunks, scores them for relevancy using embeddings, returns top-scoring chunks as context.

searchBySummarization_approach.name: (Recommended) Locate context by summarizing document
searchBySummarization_approach.description: Uses LLM-generated summaries (completion-only RAG strategy). Step 1: LLM summarizes chunks of the document — if `page`, each page is a chunk; if `outline`, an LLM generates a table of contents and each segment of the outline is a chunk. Step 2: A second LLM identifies the most relevant chunks based on the summaries, then uses their text as the context.
searchBySummarization_approach.note: Often outperforms the default approach. Useful for long documents in which multiple mentions of the same concept make finding relevant context difficult, for example, long legal documents.
